root_cause_and_implementation: Implements C1 contract Sec6 step 2 (Binding) as a new, additive, standalone service (PublicationInputBindingService), not yet wired into MarketDataPipelineService::completeHash/completeSeal -- wiring it into the live automatic call chain would newly require whole-C1 manifest completeness on every publication, which the pre-existing 58-case suite's disengaged/unseeded fixtures cannot currently satisfy (E032/E033 already found registry_versions.reason_registry.entries missing under the SQLite mirror), so it would have broken the entire existing suite; Binding therefore lands as its own provable slice first, exactly as the C1 contract phases capture/binding/seal/reader/admission as five separate implementation slices. bind($run, $publicationId, $tradeDate) locks the candidate publication and its existing md_publication_lineage_bindings row (both SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside one transaction), verifies ownership (publication.run_id === run.run_id), trade date, and config-snapshot consistency against the row V1's existing PublicationGovernanceBindingService::bind() already wrote, then requires ProducerInputCompletionManifest::inspect() to report zero missing_paths before proceeding (fail-closed BLOCKED otherwise, naming every missing path). It assembles a canonical md_publication_inputs_v2 bundle (schema_version, scope [market/product scope, requested/effective trade date, dataset start, knowledge cutoff, source/request mode, config snapshot id], components [stage_code/component_key/slot_hash/payload_hash/member_count references into the already-immutable md_run_input_captures rows, not re-embedded payloads], component_manifest) from RunInputCaptureRepository::forRun(), computes semantic_input_hash over that bundle (which does not include its own digest), and persists all four bound_input_* columns via UPDATE (the row already exists from V1; INSERT is never used, so V1's row identity/uniqueness is preserved). It independently re-derives six of V1's seven existing compatibility component hashes purely from the same captured content (never a fresh live query, never a mutable calendar/registry lookup for an earlier stage): market_structure_revision_set_hash and identity_revision_set_hash from the market_structure capture's board_inputs/rule_revisions via a faithful port of PublicationGovernanceBindingService::bindMarketStructure's own resolution algorithm; calendar_revision_set_hash from calendar_session captures filtered to the exact trade date with V1's identical supersede/knowledge-cutoff filter; status_revision_set_hash from the per-listing eligibility-expectation/v1 captures (the same $expectation EodEligibilityBuildService itself captures verbatim, so no independent re-derivation of eligibility decision logic was needed); event_revision_set_hash, source_scale_assessment_set_hash and factor_decision_set_hash from event_factor's already-captured md_adjustment_factor_decisions table. Each derived hash is compared against V1's already-stored value; any mismatch throws INPUT_CAPTURE_BINDING_COMPATIBILITY_HASH_MISMATCH naming the field, rather than silently trusting or overwriting it -- proven by deliberately corrupting a stored V1 hash and confirming Binding refuses to proceed. Idempotency: a same-content re-bind is a safe no-op (returns the existing hash); a persisted context recorded out of band that differs is rejected as INPUT_CAPTURE_BINDING_CONFLICT, never silently overwritten. Seal immutability is enforced at the application/repository level (matching the pre-existing precedent for V1's own hash columns, which likewise have no DB trigger -- this codebase's established pattern for seal-state immutability is application-level, not a DB trigger, confirmed by grep across the base schema finding zero seal-related triggers anywhere): a sealed publication whose stored hash already matches is an idempotent no-op, but a sealed publication that would require any change is rejected outright as INPUT_CAPTURE_BINDING_SEALED_PUBLICATION_IMMUTABLE. Historical mode (request_mode === replay_verify) is rejected unconditionally before any other work, matching Q2's 'no historical identity reconstructed from assumptions.'
